newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bezeq to raise $200 million in bonds.
newsitem.headline: Bezeq to raise $200 million in bonds.

text.p: Bezeq Israel Telecom said on Thursday it was preparing to offer $200 million of dollar denominated bonds in the United States, its first-ever overseas debt offering.
Spokeswoman Ella Bar-On said a delegation of company officials was currently in the United States to meet with potential underwriters and discuss details of the issue.
"Our people are in the United States right now to raise $200 million in Yankee bonds," she told Reuters, adding that the general terms should be completed in about two weeks.
She said Bezeq would use the money to exchange short term for long-term debt.

Bezeq, Israel's main telecommunications company, is 76 percent-owned by the Israeli government. Another 10 percent is controlled by Britain's Cable and Wireless Plc and the remainder is traded on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchnage.

The government is expected to make a global offering of Bezeq equity later this year. But it first wants to complete negotiations with Cable and Wireless over the future of the company's Bezeq holding.

Bezeq, which once held a monopoly of telephone service, has begun facing competition over the last five years as the government gradually demonopolises market segments. Last month, Communications Minister Limor Livnat announced that the last remaining segments of Israel's telecommunications market would be open to competition by the end of 1998.
